learnerSourceCheck.prompt: Create a rectangle of area 24 square units inside the nine-by-nine multiplication table, starting at its upper-left DATA square. Enter its number of rows and columns as two whole numbers separated by a comma (each from 1 to 9). Show and explain your drawing. More than one answer works.

supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceGoal: Let’s explore area and the multiplication table.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.sourceLearningGoals: Explore connections between area and the multiplication table.
teachingSteps: Decompose the growing dot arrays into nonoverlapping blocks.
Read the four three-row rectangles from factor headers and lower-right product cells.
Construct your own rectangle in the five-by-five table, then a 24-square rectangle in the nine-by-nine table.
Use familiar products of 2, 5 and 10 to find more facts; explain row and column patterns with equations.
Compare strategies and complete the independently authored seven-by-four Cool-down.
supplementalLessonTeachingGuidance.caution: Exclude header cells; keep each rectangle inside its specified table. Many valid rectangles and explanations are possible; do not require completion of every table cell.

firstPartyPractice.prompt: Independently draw a rectangle from the upper-left DATA square of a multiplication table, covering 4 rows and 6 columns. What product belongs in its lower-right cell? Explain how you checked the area.

independentEdulyticsCoolDown.prompt: New Edulytics task: draw a rectangle covering 7 rows and 4 columns in a ten-by-ten multiplication table. Enter the product in its lower-right cell. Draw or describe the rotated rectangle and explain how it checks your answer.

stageC.humanRubric: Check that rectangles start at the upper-left DATA square and exclude headers. The 24-square task accepts 3×8, 8×3, 4×6 and 6×4; 2×12 cannot fit the nine-by-nine table. Inspect drawings, lower-right product placement, factor-header alignment, student-authored pattern equations, notices/questions, partner explanations and optional-center work. Filling every cell is not required. A numeric answer never establishes discussion or completion of these tasks.

matchingScope: Positive bounded whole-number row/column counts and product; all four area24 orientations accepted within9×9. Independent arithmetic, swapped equations and dot totals checked; drawings and arbitrary pattern authorship always human-reviewed.

Inspect actual authenticated canonical Rich V2 and companion rendering, table headers/blank cells, screen-reader descriptions and mobile overflow.
